reason: Narrower. The 2–3 bracts that make up the spathe (as in Allium) are each an inflorescence bract, and PO lists spathe as a synonym of PO_0009054. 'spathe bracts 2–3' is a count of these bracts (pattern 03). This is not FLOPO_0986007 spathe, which is the whole structure.

An eye-like spot or gland dot that is about 0.75 mm wide, elliptic and dark brown. It could be a gland dot, a pigmented spot or a pit, depending on the family. Without the family and the organ that bears it, nothing can be grounded.

target: leaf epidermis (PO_0006016): the band-shaped region holding rows of leaf stomatal complexes (PO_0025183); 'of 15–25 rows' is a count of stomatal rows (pattern 03), and 'white' is the colour of that region
reason: This is how conifer floras describe the zone of stomata on the leaf epidermis. Only one flora uses it, so it fits better as a region of an existing class than as a new term.

reason: Guide cells are the large central cells seen in a cross-section of a moss leaf costa ('8 or 9 guide-cells'). One flora uses the term, so a cell of the costa is enough.

label: stelidium

reason: French 'stélidies' are a real, separate structure of the orchid column, described by shape (triangular, acute) and length. Mapping them to the gynostemium would give the column the wrong shape. They are widely used in orchid floras (Bulbophyllum, Pleurothallidinae). Propose to PO upstream along with gynostemium.
